transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Well, thank you. I came in because... well, I've been having these nights where I just eat. And afterwards, I just sit there with crumbs and empty containers all around me, feeling so ashamed and disgusted with myself. It's heavy on me. I feel so bad that the next morning I can hardly even bring myself to pray, or look folks at church in the eye. So, that's why I'm here.
Do you feel like you're in control of your eating during these nights?

No, I don't. Once I take that first bite after the house is quiet, it's like my good sense just steps aside. Even while I'm sitting there telling myself, 'Belinda, stop now,' my hands just keep right on reaching for more. I really don't have any control over it once it starts.
Do you feel guilty after these eating episodes?

Yes, I do. Like I mentioned when I first sat down, the shame is just awful. When it's over and I'm just sitting there looking at all the crumbs and empty containers, I feel completely disgusted with myself. The guilt is so heavy that, like I said, I can barely even bring myself to pray the next morning or face anyone at church. It just eats away at me.
Have you experienced any problems with sexual interest or function?
No, I haven't... no, I haven't noticed any problems with that. That hasn't really been an issue for me at all.
Do you usually feel hungry before these eating episodes start?

No, not really. It's not like my stomach is growling or anything. I'm usually not physically hungry at all when it happens. I just... well, I just start eating anyway. It doesn't seem to have anything to do with actually needing food.
Do you feel any better or more relieved after these eating episodes are over?
No, not at all. I don't... there's no relief. Like I was saying earlier about the guilt, I actually just feel worse. I definitely don't feel better once it's over.
Do you consider the amount of food you eat during these episodes to be excessively large?

Yes, I definitely do. It's a lot of food. On a bad night, I can start with a plate of leftover casserole from a funeral luncheon, and... well, before I know it, I've eaten that, half a pan of brownies, some biscuits, and whatever chicken salad is sitting in the fridge. Just all of it, right in one sitting.
Do you find that you're eating very quickly during these episodes?

Yes, I do. I eat so fast... usually I'm just standing right there at the kitchen counter. I barely even taste what I'm having, whether it's a piece of pound cake or a handful of crackers. Sometimes I actually catch myself swallowing the food before I've rightly chewed it. It all just goes down so quickly.
